title: Investigate and reduce generated Body skinning smear
description: The generated implicit Body mesh shows undesirable stretching/smearing when individual Body/neck bones are rotated in the editor. The current build-time authoring uses closest-point-to-segment weighting, domain eligibility, up to four influences, and a broad RadiusScale=3 falloff. Determine whether the visible deformation is caused by influence radius/overlap, segment placement, pose transform semantics, bindposes, or another skinning contract before changing the weighting algorithm. Do not solve this by disabling useful joint blending or reverting to per-frame mesh regeneration. Required investigation: capture actual BoneWeight data for dinus_uprightus; perform isolated one-bone rotation tests across Body root, spine, neck, limb attachment and terminal bones; compare observed vertex motion against the pure LinearBlendSkinning oracle; identify vertices with excessive distant/competing influences; verify bindposes/rest-pose equivalence; characterize the minimum overlap required for smooth joints; benchmark any candidate weighting change. Prefer deterministic build-time fixes and preserve the indexed zero-allocation animation path. Adversarial review must challenge world-vs-local transform semantics, parented bone rotations, bindpose space, root bone choice, four-influence truncation, tie ordering, domain eligibility, influence radius scaling, mirrored chains, body segment topology, and whether apparent smear is expected linear-blend behavior or an authoring defect.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: User-provided Unity screenshots show that Euler-angle bone edits deform the generated creature more plausibly than the built-in SceneView Rotate tool, but the implicit Body surface still exhibits visible stretching/smearing. This is a separate correctness concern from the editor gizmo pivot issue tracked by TSK-0136.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Peer audit 2026-09-08: `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.RadiusScale = 3` makes each influence reach three times the morphology radius before falloff, with squared falloff. This is a concrete testable suspect for neck/head/shoulder smear because closely packed Body segments can retain substantial competing weights across the joint. Treat as a lead, not a diagnosis: generation succeeding is consistent with over-broad overlap but does not prove it. First empirical experiment should hold topology, pose, bindposes, and domains constant and compare current RadiusScale/WeightFalloffPower against tighter radius/steeper falloff candidates on `dinus_uprightus`. Acceptance remains Unity deformation evidence plus comparison against the pure LinearBlendSkinning oracle; no constant change should be committed solely from source plausibility.
